To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of weak inversion IAs in CMOS technologies is the most energy and noise efficient approach for ECoG monitoring.
(1) ECoG monitoring instrumentation can be implemented with CMOS technology and (2) CMOS IAs operating in weak inversion offer a good compromise between power consumption, noise, and bandwidth.
(1) ECoG monitoring is feasible and practical with integrated circuits and that (2) ECoG signals can be acquired with a power dissipation of 1 µW per channel.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of low-power CMOS ICs for ECoG recording and the integration of these ICs into a wireless ECoG system.
the design of integrated circuit interfaces for ECOG monitoring systems.
the development of integrated circuit interfaces for recording ECoGs from the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CMOS technology offers a unique combination of high energy efficiency and low noise for recording ECoGs with a high signal to noise ratio.
the design of the IA is the key to the success of a high performance ECoG monitoring system.
the state of the ECoG interface technology is not yet at a point where it can be considered as a viable alternative to EEG.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the use of a CMOS IA with a CMOS lowpass filter and a CMOS comparator can achieve high energy efficiency, low noise, and high CMRR.
ECoG recording is a promising technology for monitoring brain function and that integrated circuit design for micropower, low noise, high CMRR and highpass filtering is an enabling technology.
the IA is the most important component in the signal conditioning chain for ECoG recording.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a high CMRR is not necessary to obtain high quality ECoG signals, and that the IA design can be simplified by using the CMRR as an additional degree of freedom.
CMOS IAs operating in weak inversion offer a viable alternative to bipolar junction transistors (BJTs) for ECoG recording.
a high performance, high energy efficiency ECoG interface can be obtained with CMOS technology.
